highlights.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
highlights.summary: The social media giant is accused of not informing about 20 million users it had access to their photos.
body: Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app.
The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant.
The charge is related to a feature which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts.

Facebook requested access to users' photo galleries through a single app-wide authorisation. According to the Italian regulator, a preceding notice did not make clear that this would also allow Facebook to generate suggestions based on photos in their gallery.

highlights.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
highlights.summary: Some governments moved to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations.
body: On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed.

Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry.

China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday, a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang.

highlights.title: Blade Runner Is Officially Getting The AAA Game Treatment
highlights.summary: Alcon Entertainment, which owns the Blade Runner franchise, confirmed in a recent interview that it has discussed making a AAA game based on the beloved sci-fi series.
body: We learned about the AAA game plans for Blade Runner in a recent IGN interview about the upcoming Prime Video series Blade Runner 2099. Andrew Kosove, co-CEO of Alcon Entertainment and executive producer of the show, was asked whether Alcon has spoken with game studios about making a Cyberpunk 2077 -like AAA game based on the Blade Runner IP. Kosove apparently said "yes" before adding that they'd want the game to be AAA and prioritize player interaction with the world.

Kosove didn't reveal much else, and no such project has been officially announced as of Nov. 2026. As such, we can't help but wonder whether a known AAA game studio is already working on a Blade Runner game or if the project is still in the discussion and negotiation stages. It would be amazing to finally see a game like this, though, since Blade Runner hasn't had much luck with video games in the 2020s.

highlights.title: No Pilots. Few Air Traffic Controllers. What Could Go Wrong?
highlights.summary: Normally, aviation is slow to embrace new technology—but AI has come for the skies.
body: New systems like SMART are only the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the AI aviation revolution currently underway. Take, for instance, the Cessna Caravan that took off from Buchanan Field Airport in Concord, California, and flew south to Phoenix on a calm September morning. The plane, a single-engine turboprop, then turned east to Fort Worth, stopped at Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina, and finally arrived at Dare County Regional Airport off the coast of North Carolina. The zigzag, coast-to-coast trip covered 3,200 miles; along the way, the aircraft navigated busy airspace and maneuvered to avoid storms.
None of this would be remarkable, save for one fact: The entire journey took place without a single human hand touching the plane’s controls.

Depends who you ask. “We're introducing all this new technology to improve the system, and it's going to be a disaster,” says a recently retired FAA employee. “This is literally a Pandora's box that we are going to regret.”

highlights.title: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is an Event Even if You’re Not Playing It
highlights.summary: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.
body: As I mentioned last week, I'm not playing the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time yet. I'm familiar enough with the game not to be too wary of spoilers, though, so I've been reading around it and watching the responses flood my feeds. It's been a beautiful and uplifting experience. Even from this distance, it's clearly the gaming event of the year (until next week, anyway).

Everyone's enjoying themselves. The care and joy Nintendo's Zelda team poured into this remake is infectious, and the mood is celebratory. No tedious discourse has penetrated my feeds, and everyone's initial misgivings about the art style do not seem to have survived first contact with the game itself. Wild new caricatures of familiar characters delight me as I scroll past them.

What's even more delightful is to see how directly and profoundly Ocarina of Time still connects with people, whether they're revisiting it, experiencing it for the first time, or just being reminded of it because it's in the aether.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life.
body: CSET’s Helen Toner says ‘we’re screwed’ if our AI safety plan rests on any one person being trusted to get this right.

Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman. That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely.

But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are.

highlights.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
highlights.summary: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters.
body: Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents.

Links to outside retailers’ products have already started popping up on Amazon through the “shop direct” feature it launched last year. The company also has its own AI shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping, previously called Rufus. The World Product Graph project would also be aimed at fixing issues with the AI by providing it more data. According to Reuters, an internal Amazon document on the project says “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete” and running users’ Amazon searches with the AI is expensive. Adding more data is reportedly supposed to make the system more accurate and able to use cheaper models.

Whether this actually ships is still up in the air. The internal document reportedly says the project “depends on discovering how brands organize their products on their own websites,” which could involve Amazon crawling other retailers’ sites. Reuters says it’s unclear “if or when this plan may be implemented,” but said the document on it included an October 1st, 2027 release date.

highlights.title: 8 Iconic Video Game Villains Who Were Actually Right the Whole Time
highlights.summary: Grab your gavel: Court is in session for eight of gaming’s most misunderstood villains. Their charges? One occupied planet, one erased painting, one underwater utopia gone to rot, and a truly staggering body count.
body: The case for him: The Renoir who fights you wants to keep the fantasy alive. The real one just wants his family to stop grieving inside it.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 splits its central antagonist, Renoir, into two separate people: one painted, one real. The painted-by-Aline Renoir fights alongside Aline to keep the Canvas — and everyone painted into it, including people the expedition has come to love — alive, cutting down anyone who threatens that world. The real Renoir, trapped for years and visibly aged compared to his idealized, painted double, wants the opposite: for the Canvas to end entirely, so the family he’s lost touch with can stop pouring their grief into a fantasy and start healing in reality. Pick a side, and you’re choosing which grieving father’s heartbreak gets to count as the real one.
The case for him: His possibly-understandable philosophy never changed. What did was how far he was willing to go once someone else's ambition threatened his city.
The case for her: She spends the game telling you the Jedi and the Sith are both wrong about the same thing. Neither side proves her wrong.

highlights.title: L.A.’s Most Celebrated French Chef Is Staging a Comeback
highlights.summary: Onetime culinary wunderkind (and heartthrob) Ludo Lefebvre is keeping the city’s Gallic tradition alive with a handful of new concepts.
body: Ludo Lefebvre’s French accent hasn’t thinned much since the Burgundian’s arrival in Los Angeles three decades ago. Within a year of joining L’Orangerie, then the city’s finest temple of haute cuisine, in the mid-’90s, he had become its head chef at 25 years old, serving the likes of Kirk Douglas, Frank Sinatra and Michael Jackson. Soon his talent, charm and looks catapulted him to industry awards as well as TV, including several seasons of ABC’s The Taste alongside Anthony Bourdain and Nigella Lawson, plus cookbooks like Crave, featuring a mix of recipes and chiseled pecs.

French food is no longer peerless in L.A.’s now-pluralistic fine dining scene, in which the most buzzed-about restaurants are riffing on Swedish, Korean and Mexican traditions. Compatriots such as Michel Richard and Alain Giraud once had the city saying oui, along with the town’s superstar French-trained chefs like Thomas Keller and Wolfgang Puck.

highlights.title: Tesla is inviting some people to buy a Cybercab ‘for personal use’ — but read the fine print
highlights.summary: Tesla is doubling, or perhaps tripling down on its bold claims of an autonomous future with the offer to "select customers" to purchase a Cybercab for "personal use." But the gilded, steering-wheel-free two-seater will "only be available in supported service areas" - meaning you'll only be able to…
body: Look past the $29,990 sticker price and the math — and regulatory risk — gets messy fast.

The price of a Cybercab is listed at $29,990, plus a mandatory $299-a-month “Autonomy Subscription.” Tesla’s Robotaxi account on X announced the new offer, including screenshots of the order page and the invite email. But don’t expect a fleet of personally owned Cybercabs to suddenly materialize on public roads: “Initial availability is limited,” the invitation email warns.

Tesla began offering rides in the Cybercab as part of its Model Y-powered Robotaxi service in Austin in September. The company now has 278 Cybercabs in operation, representing approximately 40 percent of its fleet, according to the crowd-sourced Robotaxi Tracker.

The inclusion of a mandatory $299/month subscription is sure to rankle some fans who may have dreamed of cruising around in a $30,000 driverless Tesla, as originally promised by Tesla CEO Elon Musk when he first introduced the Cybercab in 2024. Musk made no mention of the Autonomy Subscription at that event, though it shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise given the $99/month fee Tesla currently charges for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature.

highlights.summary: Tenerife boss Alvaro Cervera reacts to goalkeeper Jesus Owono's 12-match ban as the club prepare for their first game since the death of Jesus de Miguel.
body: Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera says that goalkeeper Jesus Owono's 12-match ban "might feel light" but he accepts that the regulations do not "specifically account for what happened".
FC Andorra's Owono, 25, was sent off after colliding with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel during the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier match between their two respective sides on 2 November.
De Miguel died the following day aged 30, and a disciplinary committee from the Spanish football federation confirmed Owono's suspension on Friday.
It was the maximum punishment that he could have received as the disciplinary committee could only consider the offence on the pitch and not "the tragic outcome of the incident".

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

body: “All those things that you read about, about why men might be lonely – they don’t maintain one-on-one friendships, or they’re not good at reaching out, or their conversations aren’t deep and meaningful – none of those issues apply to me,” she says. “I’m a very socially connected person.”

Yet Sasha often felt lonely during her first year of motherhood, even when she was surrounded by other people. (All case studies’ names have been changed.) She attributes it now to the intensity of the experience. “It’s the identity shift of your first child, having no idea of what you’re doing, learning on the fly … You feel alone.”

We’re living through a global crisis of loneliness, with the World Health Organization (WHO) declaring it a priority for public health, but it’s hard to miss that the coverage and conversation has been overwhelmingly focused on men.
Global Google searches for “male loneliness” spiked suddenly in mid-2023, and have since seen frequent surges; interest in “female loneliness”, meanwhile, has remained a trickle.

highlights.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
highlights.summary: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash.
body: After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page.

The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

The full cause of Microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

highlights.title: Daggerheart: Hope & Fear Expansion Review
highlights.summary: Critical Role’s TTRPG system, Daggerheart, puts a greater emphasis on story-telling than some of its peers. A year after the core book was released, Daggerheart offered players and Game Masters new options for telling their stories.with the system’s first expansion.
body: As someone who plays a variety of role-playing games on both sides of the GM screen, I’m always hungry for more options. More gear for my heroes to use and more vicious monsters to sic on my unsuspecting players.
Daggerheart: Hope and Fear adds a plethora of toys to the toybox, but if you weren’t a fan of the core book, don’t expect this expansion to change your mind.

Before diving into what’s new, for those unfamiliar, Daggerheart is a narrative-focused tabletop RPG system. It uses a rather handy card-based approach to help create and manage your characters and does away with the traditional initiative mechanic during combat. One of the most defining mechanics of Daggerheart, however, is its Hope and Fear dice.

These two twelve-sided dice, one representing your Hope value and the other Fear, can either cause your checks to earn you a 'Hope' resource that can be used to pull off extra special actions, or give your GM a 'Fear' point that they can spend. A proverbial "wrench in the gears" sort of treat, depending on which die rolls higher during the check. This mechanic also serves as the namesake for the system’s first expansion.

highlights.summary: From diva-like behaviour to freebie requests that never result in a review, ‘entitled’ content creators are a growing blight on small-business owners. Now entrepreneurs are calling them out. Nicole Flanagin remembers exactly the moment an influencer came after her business.
body: The 41-year-old was already having a bad 24 hours. A mother of four, Flanagin also works at a pet rescue shelter and had spent the previous day unsuccessfully fighting for a dog not to be put down. She got home exhausted and promptly conked out in bed. Then she woke up to the message.

The video began innocuously enough with a local influencer sitting in her parked car. “For those of you who know me,” she stated, “I do reviews of local businesses. One very special thing about me is I don’t make bad reviews – but I’m kinda mad right now!” The woman had just taken her child to an unnamed cafe with “animals you can pet”, only to be coldly turned away because she had got its visiting hours wrong. In the influencer’s telling, she began bargaining with staff to try to let the girl into the area where the animals were kept. No dice. Her daughter started “literally bawling her eyes out … and they were just, like, standing there staring”.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
highlights.summary: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
body: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down. “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news.

Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor, pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital.

Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition.
“Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch.

They’re not very dynamic as a wireframe, so it’s a good thing that Rockstar leads the industry in storytelling, character, and satire.

Missions burst with thematic meaning, every second an opportunity to push someone forward or revel in gags. It doesn’t really matter what you do. In GTA, a mission that largely consists of buying cargo shorts against your will can rival casino heists, mid-air hijackings, and all-out urban warfare.

Friend Request is an early storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto V. Tutorials are behind us but Trevor has yet to join the team. Retired crook Michael De Santa is in deep trouble, so he turns to his old accomplice Lester for help. The free-as-in-speech-not-as-in-beer software enthusiast seems willing to set up a new job, but first he needs Michael to blow open the walled garden that is Jay Norris’s skull.

highlights.title: ‘None of them had ever seen an eclipse in real life’: Maurice Bakley’s best phone picture
highlights.summary: An ​e​lementary school ​w​atch party turned into a great opportunity to take a child’s-eye view of a spectacular astral phenomenon. Maurice Bakley was chaperoning an eclipse watch party at his son’s elementary school in Arlington, Virginia, when he took this photograph.
body: “The boys in the photo, one of whom is my son, are part of a tight group of friends. They’ve known each other since kindergarten through their bilingual Spanish immersion school,” Bakley says. “They were eight and nine years old at the time, and none of them had ever seen an eclipse in real life.”

As the kids were sitting cross-legged on the ground, Bakley made sure to get down to their level for this shot. “A top-down angle wouldn’t have conveyed the same intimacy,” he says. “I approach mobile photography in the same way that I used to approach SLR photography, which includes being intentional in both the capture and the edit.”

When editing, Bakley applied a film-like colour grading, and a touch of blur to the background to focus attention on the boys. He also opted for a square crop. “I don’t crop in that way often,” he says, “but it suited this composition, lending a more timeless, nostalgic feeling.”
